concepts.definition: A named grammar production that binds a non-terminal to an expression.
constraints: A rule binds exactly one nonterminal name to one grammar expression.
Grammar inference and the grammar surface translation use this concept to name rules.
The English and Russian grammar surfaces translate the rule name through this concept.

concepts.definition: An ordered concatenation of grammar expressions.
constraints: A sequence matches its expressions in order, each after the previous one.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A prioritized grammar alternative where earlier matches win.
constraints: The first alternative that matches wins; later alternatives are not tried.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A grammar alternative whose branches are not semantically prioritized.
constraints: Every alternative is a possible match; none is preferred.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A grammar alternative among expressions, ordered or unordered.
constraints: A choice is either an ordered choice or an unordered choice.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A counted repetition with explicit minimum and optional maximum bounds.
constraints: The minimum count is at most the maximum count when a maximum is given.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A repetition that accepts zero or more occurrences.
constraints: The repetition also accepts no occurrence at all.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A repetition that accepts one or more occurrences.
constraints: The repetition requires at least one occurrence.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: An expression that may be present or absent.
constraints: The expression accepts zero or one occurrence of its inner expression.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A literal terminal token matched directly in the input.
constraints: The literal text is matched exactly, letter case included.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A literal terminal token matched in the input without regard to letter case.
constraints: The literal text is matched with letter case ignored.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A reference to another named grammar rule.
constraints: The referenced rule is defined in the same grammar.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A set of characters accepted at one input position.
constraints: A character class lists characters and character ranges, and may be negated.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: An inclusive range between two character endpoints.
constraints: The first endpoint is not greater than the second endpoint.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A wildcard grammar expression that accepts any single character.
constraints: The expression consumes exactly one character and fails at the end of input.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A positive lookahead predicate that tests an expression without consuming input.
constraints: The predicate consumes no input whether it succeeds or fails.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A negative lookahead predicate that rejects when an expression would match.
constraints: The predicate consumes no input whether it succeeds or fails.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A labelled or anonymous capture of a grammar subexpression.
constraints: A labelled capture carries its label as a readable name.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A grammar expression written with one of the feature union forms of docs/grammar/feature-union.md, such as a precedence, predicate, mode, byte class, macro expansion, embedded language or error recovery form.
constraints: The form keeps its own head and fields; the native executor gives it its meaning.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
The link codec carries the form as its native listing spelling.

concepts.definition: A grammar expression that accepts the empty string.
constraints: The expression always succeeds and consumes no input.
A grammar expression of this kind is one variant of the grammar expression tree.
Importers and emitters of every grammar format map it to the same concept.

concepts.definition: A grammar rule whose expression matches without implicit whitespace between its parts.
constraints: An atomic rule is a rule kind; its expression is an ordinary grammar expression.
Grammar formats without atomic rules keep the kind as a fidelity note.

concepts.definition: A grammar rule that matches without producing a parse tree node of its own.
constraints: A silent rule is a rule kind; its expression is an ordinary grammar expression.
Grammar formats without silent rules keep the kind as a fidelity note.

concepts.definition: A grammar rule whose whole match is reported as one lexical token.
constraints: A token rule is a rule kind; its expression is an ordinary grammar expression.
Grammar formats without token rules keep the kind as a fidelity note.

concepts.definition: A priority that decides which token the lexer produces when several token rules match the same input.
constraints: Lexical precedence orders token rules; it never decides between parse alternatives.
It stays distinct from syntactic precedence even where both are spelled alike, as prec inside and outside token in tree-sitter.
Grammar formats without lexical precedence keep it as a fidelity note.

concepts.definition: A priority and associativity that decide between parse alternatives when a grammar is ambiguous.
constraints: Syntactic precedence resolves conflicts between parse alternatives; it never decides which token the lexer produces.
It stays distinct from lexical precedence even where both are spelled alike, as prec inside and outside token in tree-sitter.
Grammar formats without syntactic precedence keep it as a fidelity note.

concepts.definition: A named set of grammar rules with a start rule.
constraints: Every nonterminal a rule references names a rule of the grammar.

concepts.definition: A single character listed in a character class.

concepts.definition: A character range listed in a character class.

concepts.definition: The record of how surface syntax was expanded and elaborated into core terms.
constraints: Each language frontend reports evidence for this construct or states why it is unavailable.
The construct is unavailable when no expansion or elaboration trace was produced.

concepts.definition: The project a program belongs to and the packages it depends on.
constraints: Each language frontend reports evidence for this construct or states why it is unavailable.

concepts.definition: Parse source text into a links network.
constraints: Every supported programming interface style reaches this operation.

concepts.definition: Query links in a network.
constraints: Every supported programming interface style reaches this operation.

concepts.definition: Transform query-selected links or source ranges.
constraints: Every supported programming interface style reaches this operation.

concepts.definition: Apply structural substitutions.
constraints: Every supported programming interface style reaches this operation.

concepts.definition: Serialize and load network data.
constraints: Every supported programming interface style reaches this operation.

concepts.definition: Capture immutable network versions.
constraints: Every supported programming interface style reaches this operation.

concepts.definition: Reconstruct through translation rules.
constraints: Every supported programming interface style reaches this operation.

distinctFrom.reason: Translating reconstructs a network in another language through translation rules; transforming rewrites selected links or source ranges within one network.

concepts.definition: Verify parse and structural diagnostics.
constraints: Every supported programming interface style reaches this operation.

concepts.definition: Parse a corpus program into its links network before translation.
constraints: Each translation corpus program records a digest for this stage.

concepts.definition: Check the parsed links network of a corpus program before emitting it.
constraints: Each translation corpus program records a digest for this stage.

concepts.definition: Emit a corpus program in each target language from its links network.
constraints: Each translation corpus program records a digest for this stage.
Each target language has its own digest.
